    <div>
      <h3 style="margin: 0 0 0.5rem 0; font-size: 1.35rem; color: #111;">Toward Sustainable Computing: Energy-Efficient SOT-MRAM Memory Innovation</h3>
      <p style="color: #444; margin: 0 0 1rem 0; line-height: 1.7;">
        A major breakthrough in Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Random-Access Memory (SOT-MRAM) led by Dr. Rahul Gupta and collaborators at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) in partnership with Antaios has been featured internationally. Published in <em>Nature Communications</em> (<em>"Harnessing orbital Hall effect in spin-orbit torque MRAM"</em>), the research demonstrates an over 50% reduction in energy consumption by utilizing orbital currents rather than expensive, heavy metals.
      </p>

      <h3 style="margin: 0 0 0.5rem 0; font-size: 1.35rem; color: #111;">Successful Spintronics Terahertz Emission with Full Heusler Compounds</h3>
      <p style="color: #444; margin: 0 0 1rem 0; line-height: 1.7;">
        Our study on full Heusler compound-based spintronic terahertz emitters (<em>Co₂FeAl Full Heusler Compound Based Spintronic Terahertz Emitter</em>, published in <em>Advanced Optical Materials</em>) was spotlighted by <em>Advanced Science News</em> (Wiley) with a dedicated feature video and highlighted by <em>Physics of Magnetism</em>, illustrating how high-amplitude THz emission is achieved across 0.2 to 4.0 THz bandwidths.
